evidence: RULE 1: a MEASURED offset must exist as its OWN ROW. Recording a measurement inside another row's evidence prose does not reach the resolver. Rows starting with # are skipped by jlc_rotation_resolve.py.

RULE 2 (2026-07-25, THE CORRECTION BELOW): NEVER populate a row from jlc_twin's jlc_offset. Derive it from the BOARD + JLC's cached model with an operator VERIFIED against pcbnew itself (pad.GetFPRelativePosition() vs pad.GetPosition()). jlc_twin.xform() used the wrong handedness, so every offset it reported was NEGATED: invisible at 0/180 (sign-invariant) and exactly 180deg wrong at 90/270. Six rows here were populated from it and were all 180deg wrong. Checker and checked must not share a method (canon M1).

100uF/35V polymer ELECTROLYTIC (polarized) in CAP-SMD_BD6.3-L6.5-W6.5-LS7.2-FD; usb-hub-3s-v3 C1/C2. Measured 2026-07-25: our CP_Elec_6.3x7.7 pad1 (VIN, '+') at local x=-2.700, JLC model pad1 at x=-2.670 — ALREADY ALIGNED, so offset=0 (fit by pad NUMBER, rms 0.030mm @0 vs 5.370mm @180). Board rot 90 => correct CPL 90.0, but sealed v1.4 ships 270.0 = 180deg REVERSED on a polarized cap across the 9-12.6V 3S pack: they would vent. Polarity cross-checked physically so a mislabeled model cannot fool the pad fit: JLC's silk chamfer is on the -x (pad-1) end and our footprint marks '+' on the -x (pad-1) end — both conventions agree.

No name-DB rule fired: ^AMASS_XT60PW-M is start-anchored and the vendored footprint name is not prefixed, so the offset defaulted to 0. NOTE the ledger incident 'a reversed XT60 shipped once' and part.yaml 'PAD 1 IS NEGATIVE - polarity is a PART FACT': a 2-pad collinear fit resolves 90 vs 270 only via pad NUMBERING, so this one MUST also pass the JLC order-preview human gate.
